key_insight: A hidden target updated by an online learner and projected onto the feasible inventory set is provably optimal for online inventory optimization on general bounded convex capacity sets.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical, low-complexity policy for inventory control with carryover constraints and improves regret guarantees in more realistic convex capacity settings.
method: Use a hidden target as the learner’s state, then project it onto the currently feasible order-up-to set.
Apply online gradient descent as the base learner to drive the target updates.
Exploit norm alignment so target-to-feasible-set distance behaves like a scalar queue, enabling regret analysis on general convex sets.
evidence_signal: The paper reports improved regret bounds and matching lower bounds analytically, with experiments on synthetic and real-world inventory data supporting the theory.
watch_item: Performance and proof guarantees depend on choosing the projection norm consistently with the state metric, so implementation must preserve this norm alignment.
paper_title: Optimal Hidden-Target Learning for Online Inventory Optimization on General Convex Sets
